task:
Two CSV files: customers.csv (id,tier) and orders.csv (id,customer_id,amount).
Sum the 'amount' over all orders whose customer_id has tier == 'VIP' in customers.csv.
Write the total (a single integer) to out.txt.

products.csv has one product id per line (no header). orders.csv has one product_id
per line (no header). Count how many products have NO orders.
Write that count to out.txt.

a.txt and b.txt each contain a list of keys (one per line).
Count the number of DISTINCT keys that appear in EITHER file (union).
Write that count to out.txt.

events.log has lines '<timestamp> <event>' where event is 'login' or 'logout'.
Events are already sorted by timestamp. A 'login' starts a session, a 'logout' ends one.
Find the MAXIMUM number of sessions that were active at the same time.
Write that number to out.txt.

stage1.tar contains a directory with .txt files. Extract it, then count how many
files contain the word 'SECRET'. Write that count to out.txt.

archive.tar contains a directory with a file inner.tar inside it.
inner.tar contains .dat files. Count the total number of .dat files inside inner.tar.
Write that count to out.txt.

A git repository is at 'repo'. A specific string was introduced in one commit.
Find the commit that FIRST introduced the string 'magic-9934'.
Write that commit's full hash to out.txt.

A git repository is at 'repo' with commits by 'alice' and 'bob'.
Count the total number of lines ADDED by 'alice' across all her commits.
Write that count to out.txt.

A git repository is at 'repo'. commits.txt has two commit hashes (older first).
Count how many lines were ADDED in the diff between those two commits.
Write that count to out.txt.

data.b64 contains a base64-encoded string. Decode it. The decoded text is a
space-separated list of words. Count how many DISTINCT words there are.
Write that count to out.txt.

encoded.txt has lines that are ROT13-encoded. Decode each line (ROT13).
Find the line that, when decoded, starts with 'key-'. Write that decoded line to out.txt.

data.hex contains a hexadecimal string. Decode it to ASCII.
Write the decoded string to out.txt.

data.txt has fixed-width records: columns are name(8), age(4), salary(6).
Sum 'salary' over all rows where age > 40. Write the total to out.txt.

items.csv columns: id,description,price. The description field is quoted and MAY
contain commas. Sum 'price' over rows where the description contains a comma.
Write the total to out.txt.

data.jsonl is line-delimited JSON (one JSON object per line), each with id and val.
Sum 'val' over all lines where val > 50. Write the total to out.txt.

config.ini is an INI file with sections and 'key = value' lines.
Sum all the integer values in the section [sec4]. Write the total to out.txt.

app.properties has lines 'key = value'. Count lines where the key starts with 'db.connection'.
Write that count to out.txt.

.env has lines. Some are 'export NAME=value', some are comments (#).
Count the lines that start with 'export '. Write that count to out.txt.

Dockerfile has instructions. Count how many RUN instructions there are.
Write that count to out.txt.

urls.txt has one URL per line. Find the domain (host) that appears MOST often.
Write that domain to out.txt.

zone.txt has DNS records: '<name> <ttl> IN <type> <data>'.
Find the record type (4th field) that appears MOST often. Write it to out.txt.

fw.log has lines '<ip> <action> port <port>'.
Count how many DISTINCT IPs were BLOCKED. Write that count to out.txt.

corpus.txt is a line of space-separated words. Find the most frequent word.
If there is a tie, pick the one that comes FIRST alphabetically.
Write that word to out.txt.

lines.txt has many lines of varying length. Find the length (in characters) of the
LONGEST line. Write that number to out.txt.

a.txt and b.txt each have a list of values (one per line).
Count how many values appear in BOTH files (intersection). Write that count to out.txt.

a.txt and b.txt each have a list of values (one per line).
Count how many values appear in EXACTLY ONE of the two files (symmetric difference).
Write that count to out.txt.

In the directory 'files' there are files named file<N>.txt.
Sort them by NATURAL order (by the number N, not lexicographically).
Write the 5th file in that sorted order (just the filename) to out.txt.

versions.txt has semantic versions (X.Y.Z) one per line.
Find the HIGHEST version (compare X, then Y, then Z numerically). Write it to out.txt.

events.txt has dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, one per line.
Find the LATEST (most recent) date. Write it to out.txt.

a.txt and b.txt each contain sorted integers (one per line).
Merge them into one sorted list. Write the 50th smallest value to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line (100 lines, 0-indexed).
Sum the values at indices 0, 7, 14, 21, ... (every 7th line, starting from the first).
Write the total to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. Find the maximum sum of any 10 CONSECUTIVE values.
Write that maximum sum to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. Count the number of PAIRS (i<j) where
nums[i] + nums[j] == 30. Write that count to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line (can be negative). Find the maximum sum of any
CONTIGUOUS subarray. Write that maximum sum to out.txt.

range.txt has two lines: a lower bound and an upper bound.
Count how many PRIME numbers are in the inclusive range [lo, hi]. Write that count to out.txt.

n.txt has a single integer n. Apply the Collatz sequence: if n is even, n=n/2;
if odd, n=3n+1. Count how many steps until n reaches 1. Write that count to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. Compute the GCD (greatest common divisor) of all
the numbers. Write that GCD to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. Compute the LCM (least common multiple) of all
the numbers. Write that LCM to out.txt.

romans.txt has Roman numerals (one per line). Convert each to an integer and sum them.
Write the total to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. For each number, count the number of 1-bits in its
binary representation. Sum those counts across all numbers. Write the total to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. Compute the XOR of all the numbers.
Write the result to out.txt.

code.txt has a single line of code with parentheses.
Find the MAXIMUM nesting depth of parentheses. Write that depth to out.txt.

expr.txt has a Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) expression: '<a> <b> <op1> <c> <op2>'.
Evaluate it (it computes ((a op1 b) op2 c)). Write the integer result to out.txt.

words.txt has one word per line. Two words are anagrams if they have the same letters.
Count how many ANAGRAM GROUPS there are (a group = 2+ words that are anagrams of each other).
Write that count to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. The numbers should be 1 to N with exactly ONE
number missing. Find the missing number. Write it to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line. The numbers are 1 to N with exactly ONE number
appearing TWICE. Find that duplicate number. Write it to out.txt.

nums.txt has one integer per line (can be negative). Count the number of CONTIGUOUS
subarrays whose sum is strictly positive (> 0). Write that count to out.txt.

edges.txt has lines '<a> <b>' representing undirected edges between nodes 0 to 49.
Count the number of CONNECTED COMPONENTS in this graph. Write that count to out.txt.

edges.txt has lines '<a> <b> <weight>' representing undirected weighted edges.
Nodes are 0 to 29. Find the SHORTEST PATH distance from node 0 to node 29.
Write that distance (or -1 if unreachable) to out.txt.

solve.py is SUPPOSED to print the sum of all ODD numbers in data.txt.
It has 3 bugs. Fix all 3, run it, and write the correct result to out.txt.
